summary: STAR forward pseudorapidity measurements, ALICE light-ion dihadron correlations, polarization-source-tilt scaling, Levy femtoscopy, a data-driven rapidity-to-pseudorapidity test, and generator-level nuclear-geometry inference form the heavy-ion core. Transferable AI/ML work emphasizes information-aware simulation-based inference, adequately tuned surrogate baselines, and cautious interpretation of QFT language-model benchmarks.
professional_summary: Longitudinal production, limiting fragmentation, light-ion jet-medium signatures, femtoscopic source geometry, spin-vorticity coupling, nuclear radial imaging, information-bottleneck SBI, neural-operator benchmark hygiene, and QFT reasoning evaluation.
strongest_paper: Measurement of pseudorapidity distributions from Au+Au collisions with the STAR Event Plane Detector
strongest_paper_summary: STAR provides unfolded charged-particle pseudorapidity densities across eight collision energies and multiple centralities, extending precision longitudinal-production coverage over the RHIC Beam Energy Scan.

papers.title: A Barnett-Like Effect in Relativistic Heavy-Ion Collisions
papers.short_authors: Dai-Neng Liu, Kai-Jia Sun, Jan Steinheimer, Jin-Hui Chen, Yu-Gang Ma, Marcus Bleicher
papers.abstract: Transport calculations connect global Lambda polarization to the source tilt angle extracted from two-pion femtoscopy, finding an approximately linear relation across beam energy.
papers.summary: UrQMD calculations over sqrt(sNN)=2.24-7.7 GeV link the beam-energy evolution of global Lambda polarization to the tilt of the emitting source. A quadrupolar vorticity pattern largely cancels unless the source is tilted, yielding a near-linear polarization-tilt relation that is broadly consistent with existing HADES, E895, and STAR measurements.
papers.why_it_matters: It proposes a joint, experimentally accessible geometry-spin test rather than treating polarization as an isolated observable.
papers.assessment: Strong and physically interpretable, with transport and data comparisons. The experimental correlation is not yet a uniform same-energy, same-centrality measurement: one tilt point is interpolated, two high-energy polarization points lie outside the simulated range, and the linear fit neglects tilt uncertainties.

papers.title: Measurement of pseudorapidity distributions from Au+Au collisions with the STAR Event Plane Detector
papers.abstract: STAR measures charged-particle pseudorapidity densities over 2.14<|eta|<5.09 in Au+Au collisions from 7.7 to 200 GeV using detector-response unfolding.
papers.summary: The EPD measurement spans eight RHIC energies and multiple centralities. Landau-fit hit yields are unfolded with UrQMD+GEANT3 response matrices; agreement with PHOBOS is recovered where overlap exists, with improved precision and much broader energy coverage.
papers.why_it_matters: This is a durable reference dataset for longitudinal particle production, energy deposition, and limiting-fragmentation tests across the Beam Energy Scan.
papers.assessment: The day's strongest heavy-ion measurement. The broad energy lever arm and cross-check against PHOBOS are major assets; residual model dependence from response-matrix unfolding and covariance treatment will matter for precision phenomenology.

papers.title: Jet-like dihadron correlations in OO and Ne-Ne collisions at sqrt(sNN)=5.36 TeV with ALICE
papers.short_authors: Neelkamal Mallick, Joonsuk Bae (on behalf of the ALICE Collaboration)
papers.abstract: ALICE reports multiplicity-dependent near-side peak widths and the first light-ion per-trigger associated-yield ratios, including away-side IAA in OO collisions.
papers.summary: High-pT dihadron correlations in the 2025 light-ion data show a multiplicity-dependent near-side modification and an away-side associated-yield suppression in OO relative to pp. The latter is qualitatively consistent with weaker jet-medium interactions than in central Pb-Pb.
papers.why_it_matters: Light ions occupy the crucial gap where collective behavior is established but unambiguous jet quenching remains difficult.
papers.assessment: Scientifically important but not yet decisive evidence for parton energy loss. The paper is a seven-page proceedings contribution, and ALICE explicitly leaves event-activity bias and cold-nuclear-matter effects unresolved.

papers.title: Levy-stable pion emission sources in Au+Au collisions at sqrt(sNN)=200 GeV from the vHLLE+SMASH hybrid model
papers.abstract: A vHLLE+SMASH calculation reconstructs three-dimensional pion pair-separation distributions and fits them with Levy-stable source functions.
papers.summary: For central Au+Au at 200 GeV, a single Levy form describes simulated pair separations to about 100 fm, with alpha about 1.5-1.6 and slowly increasing with transverse mass. Deviations at larger separation are associated with long-lived resonance decays, while rescattering and short-lived resonances may contribute to the non-Gaussian core.
papers.why_it_matters: It helps translate measured Levy femtoscopy parameters into specific hadronic-stage mechanisms in a realistic hybrid calculation.
papers.assessment: Useful, focused phenomenology, but currently one system, energy, centrality, model setup, and fit range. The causal attribution among rescattering, resonance feed-down, critical dynamics, and fitting choices is not yet separated quantitatively.

papers.title: Midrapidity dip and limiting fragmentation of charged hadrons from RHIC to LHC energies
papers.short_authors: Neeraj Chauhan, Md. Kaosar Ali Mondal, Amal Sarkar
papers.abstract: Measured identified-hadron spectra are used to construct the y-to-eta transformation kernel and test whether the charged-hadron pseudorapidity dip requires a dip in rapidity density.
papers.summary: Across central Au+Au and Pb+Pb data, the analysis finds that a midrapidity depression in dN/deta need not imply one in dN/dy. Generator closure exposes a possible false dip from forward-region assumptions, while current LHC coverage is insufficient to establish or exclude limiting fragmentation.
papers.why_it_matters: It directly challenges a common visual interpretation of longitudinal distributions using a data-driven rather than generator-imposed Jacobian.
papers.assessment: Methodologically careful and appropriately conservative. Its conclusions are limited by poorly constrained LHC fragmentation regions and assumed covariance/kernel families, but the null-test framing is a strength.

papers.title: Inferring Nuclear Radial Parameters from Initial-State Information in Heavy-Ion Collisions Using Deep Neural Networks
papers.short_authors: Yang Liu, Yu Sha, Xiang Fan, Yan-Sheng Tu, Shi-Lei Tao, et al.
papers.abstract: A multimodal network combines TRENTo entropy-density images with multiplicity and eccentricities to regress the Woods-Saxon radius and diffuseness of uranium nuclei.
papers.summary: On independent, denser parameter-grid tests, grouping 100 simulated events improves R0 regression to R2=0.84 overall, while diffuseness reaches R2=0.53; sensitivity varies strongly with centrality. The scan uses 8.82 million TRENTo events and a separate test grid.
papers.why_it_matters: It quantifies where nuclear radial information lives in the initial geometry and supplies a controlled baseline for later inverse modeling.
papers.assessment: A competent proof of concept, not an experimental inference. Inputs include unobservable initial entropy maps and eccentricities, with no transport, detector response, model discrepancy, nuisance-parameter variation, or comparison against simpler summary-statistic regressors.

papers.title: Intrinsic Information Rates of Summaries in Simulation-Based Inference
papers.short_authors: Vansh Bansal, Pradip Sharma Poudel, James G. Scott
papers.abstract: The paper treats learned summaries in simulation-based inference as lossy channels and derives rate-distortion bounds for posterior preservation.
papers.summary: Theory shows that the required mutual-information budget grows as posteriors concentrate and that, under common support, stochastic summaries strictly outperform deterministic ones below the exact-preservation budget. A finite conjugate example and four simulator benchmarks support the rate-matched comparison.
papers.use_case: HEP and heavy-ion SBI pipelines often compress high-dimensional events before posterior estimation. Rate-matched evaluation could expose whether an encoder architecture is genuinely better or merely passes more information.
papers.assessment: The strongest transferable ML-method paper today: it combines nontrivial theory with controlled and simulator-based validation. Practical gains on large collider events, systematic uncertainties, and calibration-sensitive downstream observables remain to be shown.

papers.title: Performance of Neural Operator Baselines on 'The Well' Dataset
papers.short_authors: Yash Pincha, Andy Dimnaku, Andrew Chiang, Adarsh Ganeshram, Valentin Duruisseaux, Anima Anandkumar
papers.abstract: A modest hyperparameter search for a Tucker-factorized Fourier neural operator dramatically improves published The Well baselines under the same wall-clock limit.
papers.summary: Using only one input timestep, tuning lowers validation RMSE below the published FNO/TFNO baselines on 15 of 17 tasks, sometimes by orders of magnitude. The central result is evaluative: lightly tuned illustrative baselines should not be treated as architectural limits.
papers.use_case: Directly relevant to hydrodynamic and transport-surrogate claims in nuclear physics, where weak baselines can manufacture apparent architecture gains.
papers.assessment: A valuable corrective with clear evidence, though it is not a comprehensive architecture study and is produced by authors overlapping the TFNO ecosystem. The lesson is about benchmark hygiene, not proof that TFNO is generally superior.

papers.title: LLMs Can Tackle High Energy Theoretical Physics, yet Gaps Remain: Part I, Quantum Field Theory
papers.short_authors: Tong Liu, Bohan Li, Gongrui Cheng, Zixiong Yu, Yulan He, Volker Tresp
papers.abstract: QFT-Bench evaluates 39 language models on 75 graduate-to-research-level closed-form QFT problems using symbolic checks and LLM judges.
papers.summary: Several frontier models exceed 95% final-answer accuracy, while error analysis still finds calculation, convention, and instruction-following failures. The paper also measures whether the displayed derivation actually supports the answer and finds nontrivial unfaithfulness.
papers.use_case: The benchmark is relevant to assisted analytic work, derivation checking, and training-domain-specific evaluators for HEP theory.
papers.assessment: Broad model coverage and some expert validation make this useful, but the headline should not be read as research autonomy. There are only 75 closed-form tasks; correctness-judge agreement with experts is 98% on a 60-response sample, whereas faithfulness agreement is only 73%, and contamination/memorization is not directly ruled out.
